title: Global Market Risks, Fertility Crisis & Navigating Uncertainty - Systematic Investor 324

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Global Market Risks, Fertility Crisis & Navigating Uncertainty - Systematic Investor 324.docx

summary: Weekly Systematic Investor podcast. Rich Brennan applies weather ensemble forecasting to trend following (a diverse ensemble of models helps in outlier regimes, hurts in calm), argues risk is vulnerability not variance and that convexity and a barbell protect against hidden risk, and discusses falling fertility as a self-correcting cycle.

coverage.note: nothing actionable: intro, small talk, ruble radar opening
ruble collapse, sanctions, weaker currency effect
alternatives demand after strong equity year, return chasing, long-term measure
narrative vs timing, November 2024 trend following performance
ensemble method and application to trend following
ensemble of trend models, number of models, exits
outliers as regime transitions, 10 vs 20 models, concentration
watch list, hidden risks, backward-looking risk models
why VaR is used, risk targeting, large fund trading

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - first reader captured the ensemble-model, hidden-risk, convexity and fertility arguments thoroughly; missed mostly Ukraine and ruble side-views, the election-reaction datum, gold's 21%, short-term CTA index data, diminishing returns of model count, the Man diversification point and the VaR-versus-stops framing.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: a weaker currency always sort of improves the export side of the equation but the import side of the equation if they're dependent on a lot of those Imports it's going to lead to significant increases in inflation
claims.claim: A weaker ruble helps exports (energy sold in other currencies yields more rubles) but raises imported inflation, leaving the central bank with policy challenges when rates are already about 22%.
claims.testable: partly - mechanism standard, impact size unknown

correction.issue: Two speakers merged. The point that energy sold to China and India may be priced in other currencies, so a weaker ruble yields more rubles, is Niels's; the import-inflation point and 'rates already at 22%, where do they go from there' is Rich's.
correction.fix: Niels: much Russian energy is sold in other currencies, so a weaker ruble gives Russia more rubles. Rich: a weaker currency helps exports but, if Russia depends on imports, it raises inflation, and with rates about 22% the central bank has little room.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I think the US came out with sanctions recently that hit that gas prom bank and um I think that's actually probably What's um you know caus a catalyst for the decline in the rubble
claims.claim: US sanctions on Gazprom Bank were the probable catalyst for the ruble collapse in November 2024.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's probably the best time now to make sure you have the Alternatives specifically Trend following in your portfolio um before things get uh crazy uh in the traditional space
claims.claim: Trend following is a core allocation that should be held regardless of equity performance, especially when equities are strong and could turn.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they'll be driven towards that short-term performance return chasing as I call it
claims.claim: Investors chase one-year performance (Morningstar-type reports) and drift away from alternatives after a roughly 25% S&P year, a lack of demand not caused by weak alternatives.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: long-term performance is the probably the best measure of um how you can manage risk and uncertainty across multiple regimes
claims.claim: Long-term performance, not 1-3 year returns, is the best measure of managing risk and uncertainty across regimes, and trend following offers protection against uncertainty.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we certainly don't worry about the why I'm not saying we can know the when in advance but we know the when when we see it when the data tells us it's now
claims.claim: Narrative explains why markets move but trend followers care about when, which they know only when the data signals it; investors given the choice would rather know when.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we never know if we as Trend followers going to be on the right side or the wrong side of that outcome
claims.claim: Before binary events such as elections or Brexit, trend followers cannot know which side they will be on; in November 2024 they happened to be on the right side.
claims.testable: partly - event outcomes untestable ex ante

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's been very concentrated as far as I can tell um it's equities and it's North American equities Canada US
claims.claim: November 2024 trend following gains were concentrated in North American equities.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the S&P 500 I think it's made 52 or or thereabouts uh new all-time highs this year so clearly very beneficial for Trend follows
claims.claim: Frequent new all-time highs in the S&P 500 (about 52 in 2024) benefit trend followers.
claims.testable: yes - count of highs vs trend returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they've just been on fire I think this month cocoa and coffee are up respectively well they're actually up about 34% each this this month
claims.claim: Softs (cocoa, coffee up about 34% each in November) and grains were big trend winners in 2024.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the benefit of not only being rules based but also being fully Diversified
claims.claim: A difficult year (strong start, weak summer, rally late) showed the value of rules and full diversification across markets.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: Bitcoin gold for me and Australian dollars um um you know coffee was marvelous orange juice marvelous
claims.claim: In 2024 outliers such as Bitcoin, gold, AUD, coffee and orange juice drove trend following returns.
claims.indicator: gold, AUD, Bitcoin, coffee, orange juice

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: one of my focuses as well is on gold and Australian dollars so um over here the two have had this marvelous marriage together
claims.claim: Gold and the Australian dollar have moved together as the gold price lifts, drawing attention to Australian gold resources.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: there has been a lot of performance dispersion in the trend following camp
claims.claim: Despite common outliers there was large dispersion among trend followers in 2024, possibly due to investment universe or strategy design.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: St in Trend up about 3% in November uh up about 1% for the year and the short-term Traders index down a quarter this month and down about 60 basis points this year
claims.claim: By late November 2024 trend indices were up only about 1-3% year-to-date versus MSCI World about 20% and S&P total return 26.8%.

correction.issue: The roughly 3% figure for the SG Trend index is the November month, not the year to date. Year-to-date figures read out: BTOP50 +3.34%, SG CTA +0.85%, SG Trend about +1%, short-term traders about -0.6%.
correction.fix: By late November 2024 CTA trend indices were up roughly 1% to 3.3% year to date (SG Trend about 1%, SG CTA 0.85%, BTOP50 3.34%) versus MSCI World nearly 20% and S&P 500 total return 26.87%.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: very much in line with what you've seen in terms of election year returns especially during uh populist period
claims.claim: The 2024 equity return pattern matched election-year returns, especially in populist periods.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: has has now replaced what we call single path deterministic models of forecasting
claims.claim: Meteorology replaced single-path deterministic forecasts with ensemble forecasts, giving probability cones for hurricanes.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: he was very confident using these single path deterministic models that they were doing but lo and behold the H the hurricane did arrive
claims.claim: The 1987 Michael Fish forecast failure illustrates the danger of confident single-path forecasts based on history.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: most of the time markets are are fairly predictable um their regime based
claims.claim: Markets, like weather, are mostly predictable and regime-based but sometimes show chaotic, nonlinear behavior.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we then use what we call a free quentis probabilistic approach which simply sums up the different possible paths and determines the likelihood of certain outcome
claims.claim: Run many simulations with slightly varied initial conditions and take probability as the share of models agreeing on an outcome.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: from a planning spec perspective this is also very important because it ensures that we have broader operations um resources being distributed wider
claims.claim: Converging ensembles justify focused resource allocation, while divergent ensembles mean high uncertainty and call for wider distribution of resources.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the constraints of that model basically dictate how how price has got to move for us to be able to remain in Trend
claims.claim: A single trend model's entry and stop parameters define the price path allowed for staying in a trend; applying an ensemble of trend models relaxes that constraint.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: when we're applying on Ensemble of models it allows this freedom of movement and it allows the fact that we might not be successful in all of our models but the balance of our models might be successful
claims.claim: An ensemble of short, medium and long trend models is more probabilistic and less prescriptive, capturing more of a trend even if some models fail.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe there's only like five or six different ways of doing Trend following really
claims.claim: Trend following has only about five or six distinct methodologies; big trends are visible so models enter at about the same time.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: where I think things are different is probably where people get out and also how they manage the risk during the trade
claims.claim: Differences among trend followers come mostly from exits and in-trade risk management rather than entries.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: but with the presence of outliers the performance of the 20 Level diversification was better than the 10 level
claims.claim: 20 trend models per market beat 10 only when outliers are present; without outliers 10 models beat 20, so the benefit of model diversification depends on regime.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I'm actually referring to these these outliers as basically being transition events between regim
claims.claim: Outliers are transition events between regimes: an abrupt break, then a new regime after the outlier settles.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we're we're actually um concentrating further into that outlier
claims.claim: More models pile into an outlier trend as it persists, giving nonlinear payoff from both the outlier and the number of systems.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: in the absence of those outli the greater L of diversification I thought impede performance and that's because of the level of whip sour the under performance Etc with the the greater number of models
claims.claim: Without outliers a larger set of models produces more whipsaw and drag, so fewer models is better.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: our process where maybe you know 30 to 40% are winners that means that in these um these environments which are free of of outliers
claims.claim: Trend following wins only 30-40% of trades, so in outlier-free periods most trades lose and less participation is better.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I clearly see in Fairly predictable regimes low levels of diversification are better than higher levels of diversification but when we get into fairly chaotic regimes higher levels of diversification are better
claims.claim: The same regime-dependent result applies to market diversification: low diversification is better in predictable regimes and high in chaotic regimes.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: one of the key reasons for his success was this willingness to take concentrated bets
claims.claim: Druckenmiller attributes success to concentrated bets, and willingness to embrace concentration and volatility pays off even though investors fear portfolios converging on one theme.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: as the trend matures more and more signals so it still is incredibly RW base
claims.claim: Ensemble trend following adds models as a trend matures, concentrating on big winners in a rules-based way rather than by hindsight; it needs concentrated risk on winners.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: a diversification of markets to me is more as opposed to an a position in all of those markets it's more a watch list uh where I'm waiting for these outliers to emerge
claims.claim: Market diversification is a watch list: take a small allocation when an outlier emerges and add as it endures, without holding positions in all markets.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: during periods of apparent Market stability risks often accumulate unnoticed beneath the surface of complex adaptive systems uh eventually erupting in what we call these disruptive events
claims.claim: Apparent calm lets risk accumulate beneath the surface until it erupts in disruptive events.
claims.testable: partly - indicators of leverage buildup needed

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: traditional risk management models such as value at risk sharp ratios even even position sizing algorithms
claims.claim: VaR, Sharpe ratios and position sizing such as Kelly use the past to allocate risk, which fosters false security and misses forward-looking vulnerabilities.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I think risk needs to be seen as vulnerability not probability
claims.claim: Risk should be defined as vulnerability (what could happen) instead of historical variance of returns.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: it wasn't the lightning strike itself the subprime defaults but it was the contagion or the systematic correlation that b the system to its knees
claims.claim: In 2008 models assumed stability of mortgage securities and missed contagion through interconnected derivatives; systemic correlation caused the crash, not the subprime defaults.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: this is very much like the financial markets you know even though we don't necessarily see the risk in our historical volatility of our models we see you know changing leverage changing asset
claims.claim: Like snow loading on a slope, rising leverage and asset concentration raise fragility while historical volatility looks calm; hidden leverage, concentration and feedback loops amplify shocks.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: so there is I believe an antidote um to this fragility found in systems and this is convexity
claims.claim: Positive convexity (disproportionate gain in favorable conditions, limited loss in downturns) is the antidote to fragility.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we saw that in the the track record of some of these fantastic funds that have collapsed we didn't see any evidence in the record
claims.claim: Standard deviation and Sharpe did not reveal warehoused risk in funds that later collapsed, which looked low-risk historically.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: but if you're using robust braking systems a driver can confidently accelerate capitalizing on those straight set while safely navigating curves
claims.claim: Strong downside protection (brakes) lets a portfolio take more risk when conditions are favorable, a dual barbell approach.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: for instance before 2020 few Models Incorporated the potential for a global pandemic halting economic activity overnight
claims.claim: Backward-looking risk metrics underweight unprecedented events such as the 2020 pandemic.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: these stable periods encourage risk-taking behaviors as investors extrapolate calm into the future
claims.claim: Volatility compression: calm periods lead investors to extrapolate calm, add leverage, tighten correlations and raise systemic fragility, like a sand pile.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: stability reduces a perceived need for protection driving down the cost of insurance like instruments such as options
claims.claim: Stability makes options and insurance cheap, though it is when they are most valuable.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the 10 best performing months accounted for 30% of total compounder growth while the 10 worst months accounted for 40% drag
claims.claim: In a 40-year S&P 500 study the 10 best months gave 30% of compound growth and the 10 worst months 40% drag, so extremes dominate returns.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: minimizing your adverse risk exposure one side of the barbell but leaving yourself open for unlimited opportunities the other side of the barbell
claims.claim: A barbell (protect against losses on one side, stay open to unlimited upside on the other) balances conservative risk management with aggressive opportunity pursuit.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: when we talk about volatility targeting and all of these methods that are designed to reduce the unfavorable volatility based on historical measures I think that's a bit um shortsighted
claims.claim: Volatility targeting based on historical measures is shortsighted compared with convex portfolio management.
claims.testable: yes - vol targeting vs convex can be backtested

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: so I think the difficulty of risk is our difficulty in quantifying it and I think this was a measure that that said hey we know what we're doing we can quantify risk
claims.claim: VaR is popular because it can be quantified and gives managers and investors a sense of control.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: in Trend following typically say volatility is not risk
claims.claim: Trend followers say volatility is not risk, while other strategies rely on volatility measures.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: set of what possibly could happen I think there is a far greater potential in the future uh risks that could emerge it we've never seen in that historical record
claims.claim: History is a small sample of possible outcomes, so future risks can exceed anything in the record.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: by flattening the volatility suppressing volatility um it makes it a very appealing product for investors
claims.claim: Large managers adopt VaR partly because smoothing volatility makes the product more appealing, even though they may know portfolios are vulnerable (LTCM).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you look at the big managers uh evolving volatility rolling 12 months volatility Etc I don't think it's stable so I don't think they target V I think they target risk
claims.claim: Large managers' rolling 12-month volatility is not stable, so they target risk rather than volatility.
claims.testable: yes - rolling vol can be checked

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: fact that you only need to do a small adjustment trade every day because if you have large AUM and you suddenly need to get out on a stop or three stops whatever you may have a much
claims.claim: VaR-based small daily adjustments suit large AUM because exiting on stops has a bigger market footprint.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: over a 10 20 year period when things haven't flooded they're very open to sort of open up land and flood prone areas for development
claims.claim: Short historical samples lead to complacency: Brisbane councils allow flood-prone development, and insurers underestimate tail events.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: there's that which can be Quantified and there's that which I feel Falls outside quantifi quantification which is what I refer to as uncertainty
claims.claim: Risk is quantifiable but uncertainty is not, and it appears at inopportune times, usually when things look stable.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they have cycles of prosperity and they have the these counterbalancing Cycles
claims.claim: Systems such as population have cycles of prosperity and counterbalancing cycles; people extrapolate recent memory, e.g. from overpopulation worries to underpopulation worries.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: nothing can have a a a sustainable average annual growth rate on this finite Planet there must be these these Cycles where we get periods of boom and periods of bust
claims.claim: Applying doubling times (rule of 70) to growth rates shows steady growth cannot persist on a finite planet, so boom-bust cycles are inevitable.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: Global fertility rates have experienced a dramatic decline falling over uh falling from over five children per woman in about the 1960s to around 2.3 today
claims.claim: World fertility fell from over five children per woman in the 1960s to 2.3, with South Korea very low, Australia 1.5 and Japan 1.4.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: coming up by 2,100 97% of countries around the world are going to face severe um short population shortages
claims.claim: Citing the WHO, he says infertility will be a leading disease and 97% of countries will face severe population shortages by 2100.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: Rising housing costs education expenses Health Care burdens these all discourage larger families
claims.claim: Housing, education and health care costs discourage large families, as seen in South Korea's high house prices and record-low fertility.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the the microplastics are causing I think they're causing sort of endocrine disrupting chemicals uh which interfere with hormone production this lowers fertility rates globally
claims.claim: Microplastics act as endocrine disruptors and lower fertility.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we've got the the Obesity epidemic um this has been a significant um impact on fertility rates
claims.claim: Obesity causes hormonal imbalances and pregnancy complications, lowering fertility; cultural shifts to career and delayed family planning also contribute (Japan about 1.4).

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: where we allowed them to overpopulate in a confined area and we'd find that there'd be a period of explosive growth and then they'd stabilize and a period of reduction
claims.claim: Lab rat experiments show explosive growth followed by stabilisation and reduction, an analogy for self-regulating cyclical population change.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: these feedback loops are these amazing things that basically self-regulate the sizes of economies
claims.claim: Feedback loops such as microplastics lowering fertility or rising living costs encouraging smaller families self-regulate population and economy sizes.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: these adaptions come with significant challenges including you know economic stagnation aging populations social instability
claims.claim: Falling fertility brings economic stagnation, ageing and social instability, which must be handled as a complex adaptive system.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: rather than adopt static Solutions we've always got to adopt adaptive Solutions flexible Solutions recognizing that the situation changes
claims.claim: Plans and solutions should be adaptive rather than static because conditions change.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: all of these economic sanctions being applied and and all of these variables sort of all interplaying together probably to cause this collapse of the rubal
claims.claim: The November 2024 ruble collapse is read as the joint result of many interacting sanctions variables in a complex adaptive system, and it adds to geopolitical uncertainty (risk of desperate moves by Russia) because escalation is running on several fronts.
claims.testable: no - narrative explanation of one episode

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: from the Western point of view if we if countries are living up to all the sanctions there really shouldn't be much trade going on
claims.claim: If Western countries respect the sanctions there is little direct trade with Russia, so a ruble collapse should matter little to Western markets, and Russian energy sold to China and India may be priced in other currencies anyway.
claims.indicator: Russia trade volumes with the West
claims.conditions: holds while sanctions are respected; back-channel trade excepted

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's interesting how the narrative is changing right now that's all I can say so I think something is changing
claims.claim: Public statements on Ukraine peace terms shifted within days (from 'on their terms' to accepting that Crimea will not return), which he reads as a sign that the Western side is preparing a negotiated settlement ahead of the change of US administration.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: Russia's probably putting a lot of its focus and and with the North Korean troops as well onto that region to try and reclaim that back before any deal was made
claims.claim: Ukraine's hold on part of Russia's Kursk region is a bargaining chip (Kursk for Crimea), so Russia is concentrating forces there, with North Korean troops, to retake it before a deal is struck under the incoming Trump administration.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: certainly another pickup uh when they announced a new first choice for for a treasury secretary
claims.claim: After the November 2024 US election equities rallied on a pro-business reading of the result and rose again when Scott Bessent was named as Treasury Secretary pick, an example of an event-driven narrative move.
claims.indicator: US equity reaction to election result and cabinet nominations
claims.testable: yes - event study around 2024-11-05 and the nomination date

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: you're right it's up strong this year up 21%
claims.claim: Gold was up about 21% in 2024 by late November, mostly late in the year, and was one of the outliers that carried trend following returns.
claims.indicator: gold price, year-to-date return (+21% by 28 Nov 2024)

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the short-term Traders index down a quarter this month and down about 60 basis points this year
claims.claim: Through November 2024 the short-term traders CTA index was down about 0.6% for the year while the BTOP50 was up about 3.3% and the SG Trend index about 1%, evidence of wide dispersion by style and horizon even in a year with big outliers.
claims.indicator: SG Short-Term Traders Index, SG Trend Index, SG CTA Index, BTOP50

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there's probably also a point in time where you don't get much benefit uh from adding more different type of models
claims.claim: Adding more distinct model types to a trend following book, like adding more markets, probably has a point of diminishing returns.
claims.indicator: number of models / markets vs portfolio Sharpe
claims.conditions: after the main five or six methodologies are covered
claims.testable: yes - Sharpe versus number of models curve

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: maybe also that could be maybe a little bit of a lock of a draw which type of model you pick depending on what environment we are in
claims.claim: Which single model type a trend follower picks may be partly a luck of the draw depending on the environment, which is an argument for holding several model types.
claims.testable: yes - rank stability of model types across regimes

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: people think that by trading more markets you actually get more diversification but actually his view was uh that it could actually be the the opposite
claims.claim: A former Man colleague argued that trading more markets does not necessarily bring more diversification and can bring the opposite, because positions in many markets can load on the same theme.
claims.indicator: number of markets vs diversification (effective bets)
claims.conditions: when markets are driven by a common factor
claims.testable: yes - effective number of independent bets versus markets traded

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: traditional risk models they they often prioritize proc ision over preparedness so um they focus for instance on volatility reduction rather than ensuring resilience
claims.claim: Traditional risk models prioritise precision over preparedness and aim at volatility reduction rather than resilience, so risk work should shift to understanding vulnerabilities and building portfolios that do well under uncertainty.
claims.testable: partly - compare vol-targeted and convex portfolios in crises

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: why larger managers would have come to the conclusion that probably VAR in whatever shape or
claims.claim: Managers use two risk frameworks, a portfolio-level VaR approach and a market-by-market stop-loss approach, and his observation from manager conversations is that larger managers have evolved toward VaR-type risk control rather than stops.
claims.testable: partly - compare VaR-based and stop-based risk control in a trend backtest

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the shift in demographics with the older population the baby boomer is getting older the younger people plac in them you you see how this is going to cause a lot of problems
claims.claim: As baby boomers age while birth rates fall, a shrinking younger cohort must support a growing older population, which he expects to cause large economic problems.
claims.testable: partly - dependency ratios versus growth and rates
